newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait turns down UAE call for Iraq reconciliation.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait turns down UAE call for Iraq reconciliation.

text.p: Kuwait said on Tuesday it had turned down a call by ally United Arab Emirates (UAE) to reconcile with former occupier Iraq.
"Reconciliation does not apply to a country like Iraq," Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah told parliament.
UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan made the call during Sheikh Saad's visit to Abu Dhabi earlier this month, he told parliament in remarks carried by the Kuwait News Agency.

"If it was a matter of one or two kilometres of (occupied) land, it (reconciliation) could have been discussed but the whole of Kuwait was occupied and gallows were erected for Kuwaiti youths," Sheikh Saad said.
"We can never forget the torture Kuwaitis were exposed to... The Iraqi regime cannot be trusted."
A U.S.-led force in the 1991 Gulf War freed Kuwait of a seven-month Iraqi occupation during which some 300 Kuwaitis were killed. Kuwait says another 600 are still being held in Iraq.
Sheikh Saad urged parliament to focus debate on security- related issues and not to divert attention "to other issues because security takes priority.
"I am here sounding the alarm bell...The Iraqi regime is a threat for Kuwait and defending this land and its people should be the top priority," he added.
Sheikh Saad also said that he told Kuwait's allies that the tiny oil-rich state sought their military cooperation to help defend the country.

"I told the Americans and the British and the friends...We do not want you to defend us but we want you to cooperate with us. If there is a warplane flown by a friend then a Kuwaiti will drive a battle tank on the ground and vice versa," he added.
After the war Kuwait signed military cooperation accords and joint defence pacts with the United States, Russia, China, Britain and France.
